metadata.title: Marginal Utility: Extra Satisfaction per Unit
metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.objective: Show total utility and diminishing marginal utility as consumption increases.
misconceptions: Total utility falls when marginal utility falls
expectedUnderstanding: Marginal utility is the change in total utility for one more unit
Marginal utility diminishes as consumption rises
Total utility can keep rising while marginal utility falls

primitives.text: Marginal utility: the extra utility from one more unit
MU(q) = U(q) - U(q-1): marginal utility is the change in total, not total utility.
The bars shrink while total keeps rising. Consume while MU >= 2; total need not fall.

checkpoints.title: Two different series
checkpoints.body: The blue line is total utility U(q). The bars are marginal utility MU(q), the extra utility from one more unit. The bars are not the total, and the line is not the marginal value.

checkpoints.title: Diminishing marginal utility
checkpoints.body: Drag q to the right. MU falls from 8.4 at q=1 toward 0.4 at q=6, while total utility keeps rising and only flattens. Falling marginal utility does not make total utility fall.

checkpoints.title: A decision threshold
checkpoints.body: The dashed line marks MU=2, a possible stopping rule: consume while the next unit adds at least 2. It is a decision rule, not a law. At q=6 the next unit adds only 0.4, yet total utility is still rising.

narration.text: The blue line is total utility; the bars are the extra utility from each additional unit.
As consumption rises, the marginal bars shrink while total utility continues to rise.
The dashed line is a possible stopping rule at marginal utility 2, not a claim that total utility must fall.

fallback.text: The upper panel plots total utility U(q) for q = 1 to 6. It rises from 9.2 to 31.2 and gradually flattens. The lower panel plots marginal utility MU(q) = U(q) - U(q-1): 8.4, 6.8, 5.2, 3.6, 2.0 and 0.4. Marginal utility is the change in total utility for one more unit, not total utility itself. The bars diminish, but total utility never falls in this example. A dashed line at MU = 2 marks a possible stopping rule: consume while the next unit adds at least 2. That is a decision threshold, not a law. Diminishing marginal utility and falling total utility are different claims.

accessibility.alt: Upper panel: total utility line rises and flattens. Lower panel: marginal utility bars shrink from 8.4 at q=1 to 0.4 at q=6. A movable q marker and a dashed MU=2 threshold show the stopping rule.
